original_acceptance: The minimum implementation consumes valid named inputs and meets the reviewed behavior cases; examples/templates alone do not establish completion.

asset_research_plan.decision: A pure comparison of two validated snapshots for the same unambiguous enrolled asset. Handle package additions/version changes and complete versus partial package lists. Service/firmware comparisons can follow after this works.
questions: Which package/service/OS changes are comparable across collector versions and incomplete snapshots?
How should duplicates, late arrivals, time skew and missing fields affect a delta?
Which inventory events can D13 consume without mistaking a failed collection for an uninstall?
Which smallest implementation answers the declared project need, and what evidence would make the extension unnecessary?
asset_research_plan.comparison: Compare with a simple set difference on complete, same-scope exports, then expose where that baseline fails on partial/failed or reordered collection.
cases: A partial listing omits a known package — Omission from an incomplete collection is not evidence of an uninstall.
A complete comparable listing confirms removal — A removal requires complete, comparable scope and stable identity.
Different asset identities — Do not manufacture a before/after history between different or unresolved identities.
consumers: C19: comparable snapshot history for evidence-quality evaluation.
C22/C23: replayable changes for contribution tests and observed service relationships.
D13: optional asset-change event input; Mahrous retains impact analysis and reassessment scheduling.
asset_research_plan.reviewers: Mahrous reviews the D13 event boundary; Omar reviews existing event/persistence compatibility.
asset_research_plan.start: Start the pure function once C03/C05 inputs are available. Full C17 reconciliation is not required; conflicting identities produce incomparable. Persist/emit through P03/P07 only when those integration contracts are delivered.
